message.content: You are sourcing real game logos for the Nxeon game-hosting marketing pages at /opt/nxeon and wiring them in. The current game tiles use generic hand-drawn glyphs (pickaxe, target, axe, wrench, paw) — replace them with the actual, recognizable game logos/icons. ## GAMES (these 5, matching the site's game plans) Minecraft, Counter-Strike 2 (CS2), Valheim, Rust, Palworld. ## STEP 1 — get the logo assets Use WebSearch/WebFetch to find clean, square-ish official or widely-used logo/icon images for each game. Good sources: Wikimedia Commons (official logo files), the games' press/brand kits, Steam CDN header/icon assets, or well-known icon sets. Prefer SVG; PNG with transparent background is fine. Then download each into `/opt/nxeon/public/games/` using curl (the scratchpad or public dir). Name them exactly: `minecraft.svg`/`.png`, `cs2.*`, `valheim.*`, `rust.*`, `palworld.*`. - Verify each downloaded file is a real image (check file size > 1KB and `file ` reports an image/SVG, not an HTML error page). Re-try a different source if a download is broken. - Keep them reasonably small (icons, not huge banners). If you can only find a wordmark, that's acceptable but a square icon is preferred. - These are third-party trademarks displayed nominatively to advertise game hosting (standard in the industry) — just get clean, correct, recognizable marks. If you genuinely cannot find a usable asset for one game after trying multiple sources, note it and leave that one with the existing glyph fallback. ## STEP 2 — wire them into the tiles Two files hardcode game metadata with glyph SVGs — replace the glyph with an `` of the downloaded logo: - `components/marketing/GameServers.tsx` (look for its GAME_META / game list with glyphs + gradients) - `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx` (its GAME_META with glyphs) Render each logo as e.g. `` inside the existing icon chip (keep the rounded chip container, drop the gradient glyph). Keep everything else (names, prices, layout) intact. Match how both files structure their tiles so the site stays consistent. ## RULES - Only edit those two component/page files and add files under public/games/. Do NOT touch other shared files (primitives, header, footer, globals, icons.tsx, app/page.tsx). - Do NOT run next build, tsc, prisma, or git commit. - If a logo has a transparent background it will sit on a dark navy card — ensure it's still visible (light/colored marks are fine; if a logo is pure dark, keep its chip background lighter or note it). When done, report: which logos you downloaded (source + file + size) for each game, which (if any) you couldn't source and left as glyphs, and exactly what you changed in the two files. Do not build or commit.

Everything is wired and verified. ## Logos downloaded (all in `/opt/nxeon/public/games/`) | Game | File | Size | Source | Notes | |------|------|------|--------|-------| | Minecraft | `minecraft.svg` | 2.5 KB | Reused the existing clean green wordmark already in `public/logos/minecraft.svg` | Green on navy = visible | | Counter-Strike 2 | `cs2.svg` | 5.4 KB | Wikimedia Commons `File:Counter-Strike_2_logo.svg` | Official CS2 wordmark. It shipped as dark navy `#1E202F` (invisible on the navy card), so I **recolored the fill/stroke to light `#EDF0F7`** so it reads on the dark tile | | Valheim | `valheim.png` | 314 KB | Steam CDN `apps/892970/logo.png` | Official transparent metallic wordmark. Caveat: Valheim's current Steam logo carries a small "The Bog Witch" DLC subtitle; "VALHEIM" dominates and is clearly recognizable. Couldn't source a subtitle-free clean version (Wikimedia 404, SteamGridDB 403, press-kit only behind a Drive folder). Left as-is | | Rust | `rust.png` | 26 KB | Steam CDN `apps/252490/logo.png` | Red square emblem + gray "RUST" wordmark, transparent; visible on navy | | Palworld | `palworld.png` | 109 KB | Steam CDN `apps/1623730/logo.png` | White transparent wordmark; visible on navy | All files verified as real images via `file` (SVG/PNG, not HTML error pages) and all > 1 KB. No game was left on a glyph fallback among the 5 requested. Note: **Terraria** also exists in both files' game metadata but wasn't in the 5-game scope, so I left it with its original emoji glyph + gradient (the code falls back automatically when `logo` is absent). ## Code changes (only the two files + `public/games/`) **`components/marketing/GameServers.tsx`** - Added optional `logo?: string` to the `TITLES` type and set `logo` paths on the 5 games (Terraria left without one). - In the tile's icon chip: when `logo` is set, drop the gradient/glyph and render `` inside the same rounded chip, giving the chip a neutral `bg-white/[0.06] p-2`. Glyph/gradient path retained as the fallback (Terraria). **`app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx`** - Added `logo?: string` to `GAME_META` and set `logo` on the 5 games. - Applied the same conditional img-vs-glyph rendering in **both** chip sites: the "Supported games" grid (`h-14 w-14`, img `h-9 w-full`) and the per-game pricing headers (`h-12 w-12`, img `h-8 w-full`). The unknown-family fallback (`glyph: "🎮"`) and Terraria still render their glyph since they have no `logo`. Chips use a neutral `bg-white/[0.06]` container (instead of a per-game color gradient) so every transparent mark — light (CS2/Palworld), colored (Rust/Minecraft), and metallic (Valheim) — stays legible on the dark navy card. Used `w-full object-contain` rather than the suggested `w-8` so the wide wordmarks use the full chip width instead of shrinking to a thin strip. No build, tsc, prisma, or git commit was run.
